best_architecture: Recommended architecture for Local-Claw: a LangGraph StateGraph (nodes + conditional edges over a single JSON-serializable State object) layered on top of a hierarchical Goal Tree, with a thread_id-scoped MongoDB checkpointer (langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb's AsyncMongoDBSaver, to match the asyncio orchestrator). The checkpointer persists a snapshot of graph state at every super-step, which is exactly what delivers the three properties Local-Claw needs: crash survival, resume-from-last-step, and human-in-the-loop pauses via interrupt(). Resume is just re-invoking the graph with the same thread_id. Design decisions that matter most, in priority order: (1) JSON-serializable state ONLY -- the State TypedDict holds plain dicts/lists/strings/enum values, never Python objects, coroutines, DB clients, or file handles, because the checkpointer serializes state to MongoDB at every super-step. (2) Idempotent transitions -- every node that performs an irreversible side effect (git commit/push, file write, API call) first checks a step-completed marker and skips if already done; it writes a step-started marker before the side effect and a step-completed marker after, so a crash-and-resume re-execution of the same in-flight node does not duplicate the effect. (3) An explicit status enum (PENDING -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED/FAILED/BLOCKED, plus AWAITING_APPROVAL) on every goal, with timestamps and an attempt counter, so the router can branch on status and a TTL sweep can detect goals deadlocked in IN_PROGRESS after an orchestrator crash. (4) The Goal Tree as the long-horizon plan: each node {id, parent_id, children, description, status, result, error, attempts}, decomposed top-down (mirroring ReAcTree's sequence/fallback/parallel control-flow nodes and GoalAct's global-plan-then-hierarchical-execute split). (5) Separate the short-term checkpoint state (in the MongoDBSaver collection, thread-scoped, prunable) from long-term vector memory (a separate MongoDBStore / chroma / faiss collection that survives across threads) -- conflating them bloats checkpoints and breaks replay. (6) Event-driven checkpointing at node/super-step boundaries (LangGraph default), not ad-hoc saves. The single most critical design element is the conditional-edge router: it encodes all branching, retry-on-FAILED, escalate-to-human-on-BLOCKED, and loop-back-to-plan logic, and it must read state that has actually been committed in a prior super-step, not stale pre-update values within the current super-step.
reference_papers: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al. 2022) — arxiv:2210.03629. The reason+act loop that forms the body of each agent/execute node.

Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning (Shinn et al. 2023) — arxiv:2303.11366. Self-reflection on FAILED transitions to populate the goal's error field and adjust the next attempt; backs the reflect node and attempt counter.
Plan-and-Solve Prompting (Wang et al. 2023) — arxiv:2305.04091. Decompose-then-execute; basis for separating a plan node from execute nodes.

ReAcTree: Hierarchical LLM Agent Trees with Control Flow for Long-Horizon Task Planning (Choi et al. 2025) — arxiv:2511.02424 (AAMAS 2026). Dynamically expanded agent tree with sequence/fallback/parallel control-flow nodes plus episodic + working memory; the closest published match to the Goal Tree design. On WAH-NL reaches 61% goal success with Qwen2.5-72B vs ReAct's 31%.

GoalAct: Enhancing LLM-Based Agents via Global Planning and Hierarchical Execution (Chen et al. 2025) — arxiv:2504.16563 (NCIIP 2025 Best Paper). Global plan + hierarchical execution split; informs the plan-then-execute layering over the Goal Tree.
Task Memory Engine for Spatial Context (Ye et al. 2025) — arxiv:2504.08525. Structured task-state memory beyond linear context; informs the State vs Goal-Tree vs long-term-memory separation.

SagaLLM: Context Management, Validation, and Transaction Guarantees for Multi-Agent LLM Planning (Chang, Stanford, 2025) — arxiv:2503.11951. Gold-standard transactional pattern: modular checkpointing + compensating transactions to restore system-wide consistency on partial failure (relaxed ACID). Directly motivates the idempotency guards and rollback design.

key_libraries: langgraph (Python, >=0.2) - StateGraph engine, conditional edges, interrupt()/Command resume, time-travel.

langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb (Python) - MongoDBSaver / AsyncMongoDBSaver; persists thread-scoped checkpoints to MongoDB; also exposes MongoDBStore for namespaced long-term memory. Use the async saver to match the asyncio orchestrator; call .setup() once.
pymongo / motor (Python) - MongoDB driver; motor (async) pairs with AsyncMongoDBSaver under asyncio.
pydantic (Python, v2) - validate and serialize state payloads and Goal nodes; enforce transition invariants with @model_validator; keep all models JSON-serializable (model_dump(mode='json')).

burr (apache-burr, Python) - alternative state-machine engine with observability UI; install 'burr[start]' for the local UI. Use as a lighter alternative if LangGraph's surface area is more than needed.
chromadb or faiss-cpu (Python) - long-term vector memory store, kept strictly separate from the checkpoint state.
orjson (Python) - fast JSON (de)serialization for any out-of-band artifact/event files; handles datetime/UUID/Enum natively.
pitfalls: Non-serializable state: storing Python objects, coroutines, open file handles, or a Mongo client inside the State dict causes a serialization error the moment the checkpointer writes at a super-step. Allow only plain JSON types (str/int/float/bool/list/dict/None and enum values).

Missing idempotency guard: on crash+resume LangGraph re-executes the node that was in flight; without a step-started/step-completed marker the agent duplicates a git commit, re-sends an API call, or rewrites a file. Persist the marker BEFORE the side effect and short-circuit if it already exists.

Unbounded Goal Tree growth: the tree accumulates thousands of nodes across sessions and is never pruned, bloating the MongoDB checkpoint document and slowing every load. Prune/archive COMPLETED subtrees and cap depth.

Conditional-edge logic drift: the router reads a state key not yet committed in the current super-step, producing stale routing and the wrong branch. Route only on values written in a prior super-step.
Subgraph state-isolation failure: a child subgraph mutates parent state fields directly instead of returning a scoped delta, corrupting the parent. Scope state per subgraph and merge explicitly.

Missing human-in-the-loop interrupt: the agent performs an irreversible action (rm, force-push, prod deploy) with no AWAITING_APPROVAL gate. Wrap irreversible actions in an interrupt()/breakpoint node.

Status deadlock: a goal stuck in IN_PROGRESS after an orchestrator crash with no TTL/timeout is never retried. Add a TTL sweep that resets stale IN_PROGRESS goals to PENDING (or FAILED) past a deadline.

Parallel-node races: two nodes write the same state key in one super-step, giving non-deterministic last-writer-wins. Use reducer-annotated channels (e.g. Annotated[list, operator.add]) or disjoint keys for parallel branches.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: Crash-resilient agent state machine

  Scenario: Checkpoint and resume after orchestrator crash
    Given the agent has completed step 3 of a 7-step goal
    And each completed step was checkpointed to MongoDB under its thread_id
    When the orchestrator process crashes and is restarted
    Then the agent loads the latest checkpoint for that thread_id
    And it resumes execution from step 4
    And it does not re-run steps 1 through 3

  Scenario: Idempotent retry of a failed step with a side effect
    Given step 5 performs a git commit and failed on its first attempt after committing
    And a step-completed marker for step 5 was written before the failure surfaced
    When step 5 is retried on resume
    Then the node sees the step-completed marker and skips the git commit
    And no duplicate commit is created
    And the goal advances to step 6

  Scenario: Human-in-the-loop gate before an irreversible action
    Given the agent is about to run "git push" to a remote
    When the push node sets the goal status to AWAITING_APPROVAL and calls interrupt()
    Then graph execution pauses and the current state is checkpointed
    And no push occurs until a human resumes the thread with an approval
    And on rejection the goal transitions to BLOCKED instead of pushing

  Scenario: SagaLLM-style compensation on late failure
    Given steps 1 through 5 succeeded and produced side effects
    And step 6 fails irrecoverably
    When the compensating transaction runs
    Then the registered compensations for steps 5 down to 1 execute in reverse order
    And the system-wide state is restored to its pre-goal condition
    And the goal status is set to FAILED with the error recorded
optimal_implementation:
State and Goal Tree (JSON-serializable only):

```python
from enum import Enum
from typing import Annotated, Optional, TypedDict
from operator import add

class Status(str, Enum):
    PENDING='PENDING'; IN_PROGRESS='IN_PROGRESS'; COMPLETED='COMPLETED'
    FAILED='FAILED'; BLOCKED='BLOCKED'; AWAITING_APPROVAL='AWAITING_APPROVAL'

class Goal(TypedDict):
    id: str; parent_id: Optional[str]; children: list[str]
    description: str; status: str; result: Optional[str]
    error: Optional[str]; attempts: int
    started_at: Optional[str]; updated_at: Optional[str]

class State(TypedDict):
    session_id: str
    goal_tree: dict[str, Goal]          # id -> Goal
    current_goal_id: Optional[str]
    step_markers: dict[str, str]        # step_id -> 'started'|'completed'  (idempotency)
    messages: Annotated[list, add]      # reducer-safe append for parallel nodes
    error: Optional[str]
```

Goal Tree CRUD helpers (pure functions over the dict, no side effects):

```python
def create_goal(tree, gid, parent_id, desc):
    tree[gid] = Goal(id=gid, parent_id=parent_id, children=[], description=desc,
                     status=Status.PENDING, result=None, error=None, attempts=0,
                     started_at=None, updated_at=None)
    if parent_id: tree[parent_id]['children'].append(gid)
    return tree

def update_status(tree, gid, status, **kw):
    g = tree[gid]; g['status'] = status; g['updated_at'] = now_iso()
    for k, v in kw.items(): g[k] = v
    return tree

def get_ready_goals(tree):  # PENDING leaves whose children are all COMPLETED (or none)
    return [g for g in tree.values() if g['status'] == Status.PENDING and
            all(tree[c]['status'] == Status.COMPLETED for c in g['children'])]
```

Idempotency guard pattern inside any side-effecting node:

```python
def execute_node(state):
    sid = state['current_goal_id']
    if state['step_markers'].get(sid) == 'completed':
        return {}                                   # already done; skip side effect
    markers = {**state['step_markers'], sid: 'started'}
    result = do_side_effect(...)                    # git commit / file write / API call
    markers[sid] = 'completed'
    return {'step_markers': markers,
            'goal_tree': update_status(state['goal_tree'], sid, Status.COMPLETED, result=result)}
```

Graph wiring with conditional router, human interrupt, and Mongo checkpointer:

```python
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END
from langgraph.checkpoint.mongodb.aio import AsyncMongoDBSaver
from langgraph.types import interrupt

def plan(state): ...        # decompose current goal into child Goals
def check(state): ...       # validate result; set COMPLETED/FAILED
def reflect(state): ...     # Reflexion-style; bump attempts, set error
def approval(state):        # human gate before irreversible actions
    decision = interrupt({'action': 'git push', 'goal': state['current_goal_id']})
    new = Status.IN_PROGRESS if decision == 'approve' else Status.BLOCKED
    return {'goal_tree': update_status(state['goal_tree'], state['current_goal_id'], new)}

def router(state):
    g = state['goal_tree'][state['current_goal_id']]
    if g['status'] == Status.FAILED and g['attempts'] < 3: return 'reflect'
    if g['status'] == Status.AWAITING_APPROVAL: return 'approval'
    if get_ready_goals(state['goal_tree']): return 'execute'
    return END

b = StateGraph(State)
b.add_node('plan', plan); b.add_node('execute', execute_node)
b.add_node('check', check); b.add_node('reflect', reflect); b.add_node('approval', approval)
b.add_edge(START, 'plan'); b.add_edge('plan', 'execute'); b.add_edge('execute', 'check')
b.add_conditional_edges('check', router, ['execute', 'reflect', 'approval', END])
b.add_edge('reflect', 'execute'); b.add_edge('approval', 'execute')

async with AsyncMongoDBSaver.from_conn_string(MONGO_URI, db_name='localclaw') as cp:
    graph = b.compile(checkpointer=cp)
    cfg = {'configurable': {'thread_id': session_id}}
    await graph.ainvoke(initial_state, cfg)         # resume = re-invoke same thread_id
```

Ops notes: call cp.setup() once to build indexes; run a periodic TTL sweep that resets goals stuck in IN_PROGRESS past a deadline back to PENDING; archive COMPLETED subtrees out of goal_tree to keep the checkpoint document small; keep long-term vector memory in a separate store, never in State. For SagaLLM compensation, register a compensating callable per side-effecting step and, on late failure, run them in reverse order before setting the goal FAILED.
sota_improvements: Apache Burr as a lighter alternative: in-process state machine with no heavy framework dependency, a built-in observability UI, state snapshots, and time-travel replay; prototype it if LangGraph's surface area exceeds what Local-Claw needs.

LangGraph time-travel: replay execution from any past checkpoint (get_state_history) to reproduce and debug an agentic failure deterministically, and fork from a past state to try an alternate branch.
LangGraph Studio visual debugger: inspect committed state at each node, step through super-steps, and edit state mid-run during development.

SagaLLM transactional pattern as the rollback gold standard: register a compensating transaction for every side-effecting step and run compensations in reverse order on late failure, giving workflow-wide consistency without full ACID.

Event sourcing the state: store an append-only event log of transitions alongside the mutable checkpoint snapshots for a perfect audit trail and replay-from-any-point; LangGraph's per-super-step checkpoints already approximate this, and an explicit event collection makes Local-Claw fully reconstructable after any crash.
